result.summary: On branch check/reassortment, the uncommitted working-tree diff (881 lines: README.md +114/-0 net additions, all_hanta.py +620/-46) adds a new opt-in phylogenetics stage to all_hanta.py, gated so the default pipeline path is unchanged when the flag is absent. It introduces: a CDS-nucleotide FASTA parser (parse_cds_fasta, built on a new shared _iter_fasta_records generator that parse_fasta was refactored to reuse); three-way candidate selection (collect_phylo_candidates: human-affecting-or-likely via is_human_affecting_or_likely, divergence-candidate via the existing k-mer diagnostic's requires_phylogenetic_confirmation flag, and complete-triplet isolates, unioned, then hard-filtered to require CDS present for all of S/M/L via select_primary_cds, excluding lab/vaccine-derived and unclassified/genus-only isolates); per-species/per-segment MAFFT alignment (run_mafft) and IQ-TREE ML tree building (run_iqtree) invoked via subprocess with explicit seqtype DNA; tree-based divergence diagnostics (tree_divergence_for_species, _patristic_distance_matrix, sharing rank-normalization helpers _rank_positions/_sl_m_rank_metrics with the existing k-mer compute_segment_divergence path); bootstrap-gated reassortment call classification (classify_reassortment_call, bootstrap_support_for_pair) using fixed thresholds M_OFFSET_HIGH/SL_SEPARATION_LOW; and Robinson-Foulds tree comparison via dendropy in _analyze_species. New CLI args (mafft-bin, iqtree-bin, phylo-min-taxa, bootstrap, min-bootstrap-support, phylo-seed, phylo-threads plus the phylogenetics flag itself) and a new output table ortho_reassortment_table.parquet plus output/phylogenetics/<species>/<segment>/ artifacts are wired into run_pipeline only inside the conditional phylogenetics branch. README.md is updated in parallel with a new phylogenetics setup/usage section, an expanded Reassortment section explaining the opt-in replacement for the withdrawn classifier, an output-table row, a risk-score note that reassortment_call is not yet wired into scoring, and revised Known limitations bullets. Also present in the working tree but out of the user-specified diff scope: modified output parquet files and ortho_pipeline.log (regenerated from the successful end-to-end run), plus untracked MyReport.md and output/ortho_reassortment_table.parquet and output/phylogenetics/ (run outputs) -- these were excluded per the exact pathspec the user specified restricting the diff to only all_hanta.py and README.md.
result.conventions: No CLAUDE.md files were found anywhere applicable to this review: not at the user level (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md does not exist), not at the repo root (CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md do not exist at /home/victorfrankestein/Documents/Orthohantavirus), and a repo-wide find for CLAUDE.md/CLAUDE.local.md returned nothing. Both changed files (all_hanta.py, README.md) live at the repo root, so there are no intermediate ancestor directories to check either. The reviewer should rely on in-repo conventions visible directly in the diff/file instead: the module's existing error-isolation pattern (transform_one_record-style per-unit failure isolation, now mirrored by the new per-species analysis function's try/except), the existing docstring-heavy style explaining why not just what, the project's stated principle of never silently dropping records (every candidate isolate must appear exactly once in the output table with a status), and the hard requirement that phylogenetics-only imports (Bio.Phylo, dendropy) stay lazy/deferred so a default (no phylogenetics flag) run never needs them installed or touches them at all -- any top-level unconditional import of these would violate the stated byte-for-byte-unaffected default behavior constraint and should be flagged.

candidates.summary: The opt-in --phylogenetics block was inserted before the 'Writing outputs' section instead of after it, so any exception/SystemExit raised while running the phylogenetics stage (missing mafft/iqtree binaries, missing biopython/dendropy, or any bug in parse_cds_fasta/collect_phylo_candidates/run_phylogenetics_stage) aborts run_pipeline before a single one of the standard parquet/json outputs (ortho_accession_table, ortho_species_table, ortho_isolate_table, ortho_risk_table, ortho_ml_*, ortho_qc_report, ortho_summary.json, etc.) is written.
candidates.failure_scenario: A user runs `python all_hanta.py --phylogenetics` in an environment where mafft/iqtree aren't on PATH (or biopython/dendropy aren't installed) -- exactly the setup mistake the README explicitly warns about ('don't just prepend that env's bin/ to PATH'). resolve_binary()/the ImportError check in run_phylogenetics_stage raises SystemExit, which propagates uncaught out of run_pipeline and main(). Because 'logging.info("Writing outputs")' and every safe_write_parquet/safe_write_json call for the core (non-phylogenetics) tables now sit textually after the `if args.phylogenetics:` block, none of them execute: the entire run produces zero output tables (not even ortho_summary.json), even though this feature is documented and designed to be strictly additive/opt-in and the core pipeline is supposed to be unaffected by it. The user loses the whole run over an unrelated, easily-fixed environment issue instead of just missing ortho_reassortment_table.parquet.

candidates.summary: The per-species try/except in _analyze_species only wraps run_mafft/run_iqtree, not Phylo.read, the patristic-distance/RF computation, or bootstrap-support lookup, so it only partially re-establishes the 'never aborts the run' invariant it claims (and that transform_one_record's whole-body try/except actually delivers) for a phylogenetics-stage isolate.
candidates.failure_scenario: For a species whose IQ-TREE tree is missing a tip that write_segment_fasta wrote (e.g. IQ-TREE silently dropped a duplicate/near-identical sequence during ModelFinder, a known IQ-TREE behavior with `--seqtype DNA` on near-identical CDS), _patristic_distance_matrix's `clades[labels[i]]` lookup (line ~2364, called via tree_divergence_for_species at line 2507) raises KeyError outside the try/except. Because run_phylogenetics_stage (line 2555) and its caller in run_pipeline (line 3294) have no surrounding try/except either, the KeyError propagates uncaught and crashes the whole pipeline run -- not just marking that species 'failed' as documented in the docstring/README, but losing the run entirely, including the ortho_accession_table/species/isolate/ML parquet writes that come after this block (lines 3301+).

candidates.summary: bootstrap_support_for_pair's next(tree.find_clades(name=...)) is unguarded and can raise StopIteration, which likewise escapes past the narrow try/except and aborts the run instead of failing just that species.
candidates.failure_scenario: If the M-tree's Newick file uses a tip-name variant Biopython doesn't match exactly (or if classify_reassortment_call's row['tree_m_nearest'] label doesn't correspond to an actual terminal, e.g. due to an off-by-one in label construction under partial-failure conditions), next(...) on an empty generator raises StopIteration inside classify_reassortment_call's call at line 2530, which is outside the try/except in _analyze_species and has no handler anywhere up the call chain to run_pipeline, so the whole pipeline invocation crashes and no output parquet files (default or phylogenetics) are written for that run, contradicting the 'a species/segment failure never aborts the run' guarantee documented in the function's docstring and the README's 'Nothing is silently dropped' claim.

candidates.summary: _analyze_species only wraps the MAFFT/IQ-TREE subprocess calls in try/except; the downstream Phylo.read, tree_divergence_for_species, dendropy RF computation, and classify_reassortment_call/bootstrap_support_for_pair calls (lines 2504-2536) run outside any exception handler, and run_pipeline has no try/except around run_phylogenetics_stage either.
candidates.failure_scenario: If any post-alignment step raises for a given species -- e.g. bootstrap_support_for_pair's `next(tree.find_clades(name=label_a))` (line ~2416) hitting StopIteration on a tip-label/tree mismatch, Phylo.read failing on an unexpected treefile format, or dendropy's shared TaxonNamespace/encode_bipartitions choking on a degenerate tree -- the exception propagates uncaught through _analyze_species -> run_phylogenetics_stage -> run_pipeline -> main(), which has no top-level try/except. Because run_pipeline (as of this diff) runs the entire `if args.phylogenetics:` block *before* 'Writing outputs' (line ~3290), the crash aborts the whole pipeline and no parquet tables at all are written for that invocation -- not just the reassortment table but ortho_accession_table, ortho_species_table, ortho_isolate_table, ortho_ml_feature_matrix, etc. -- directly contradicting the stated invariant ('a species/segment failure never aborts the run, it just marks that species' isolates failed and moves on') and README's 'Nothing is silently dropped' / 'a species/segment failure never aborts the run' claims for a run enabling --phylogenetics on real-world data with any edge-case tree.

candidates.summary: The per-species try/except in _analyze_species only wraps run_mafft/run_iqtree, not the Phylo.read/tree-distance/dendropy-RF/bootstrap-lookup code that follows, and run_pipeline sequences the whole --phylogenetics stage before the 'Writing outputs' block with no enclosing try/except anywhere up to main().
candidates.failure_scenario: If IQ-TREE succeeds but the .treefile can't be parsed by Bio.Phylo (unexpected characters, IQ-TREE writing an unrooted trifurcation Newick variant it doesn't like, truncated write on a full disk), or dendropy.Tree.get()/treecompare.symmetric_difference chokes because the three trees' tip sets don't line up exactly, or bootstrap_support_for_pair's `next(tree.find_clades(name=...))` raises StopIteration for a missing tip -- none of that is caught. The exception propagates out of _analyze_species, out of run_phylogenetics_stage, and out of run_pipeline uncaught, crashing the whole program with a traceback. Because this block (all_hanta.py lines ~3290-3298) runs before `logging.info("Writing outputs")` and all the safe_write_parquet calls for ortho_accession_table, ortho_species_table, ortho_isolate_table, ortho_risk_table, the ML tables, etc., a single species hitting this gap means a --phylogenetics run produces ZERO output files at all -- not just a missing/failed reassortment row for that species -- directly contradicting the code's own docstring ('a species/segment failure never aborts the run... the same per-unit error isolation transform_one_record uses') and the README's 'nothing is silently dropped' / byte-for-byte-unaffected-default claims, since the only way to get any output on a --phylogenetics run is for every single one of potentially dozens of species-level tree builds to hit no post-tree-build exception at all.

candidates.summary: _phylo_row hardcodes n_taxa_in_tree=0 for 'species_below_min_taxa' rows instead of the species' actual candidate count.
candidates.failure_scenario: A user filtering ortho_reassortment_table.parquet on n_taxa_in_species_tree to see how close an excluded species was to the --phylo-min-taxa threshold (e.g. to decide whether to lower it and re-run) sees 0 for every below-threshold species regardless of whether it had 1 candidate or phylo_min_taxa-1 candidates, silently discarding information that group_candidates_by_species already computed (it logs 'only {len(members)} candidate(s), need {min_taxa}' but that count never reaches the per-isolate output row).

verdicts.evidence: all_hanta.py lines 3290-3301: the `if args.phylogenetics:` block (which calls `run_phylogenetics_stage(...)` at line 3294) sits textually before `logging.info("Writing outputs")` at line 3301 and all the `safe_write_parquet`/`safe_write_json` calls for the core tables (lines 3302-3317, including `ortho_summary.json`). There is no try/except around this block in run_pipeline. Inside run_phylogenetics_stage (line 2555), missing biopython/dendropy triggers `raise SystemExit(...)` at line 2568, and missing mafft/iqtree triggers `resolve_binary()` (line 2305) to `raise SystemExit(...)` at line 2310 -- both uncaught, both reachable before any core output table is written. So `python all_hanta.py --phylogenetics` in an environment lacking mafft/iqtree/biopython/dendropy on PATH aborts the whole pipeline with zero output tables written, not just a missing reassortment table.

The try/except at all_hanta.py:2496-2503 wraps only run_mafft/run_iqtree; `trees[segment] = Phylo.read(...)` (line 2504) and the subsequent `tree_divergence_for_species(labels, trees)` call (line 2507) run unguarded. Inside it, `_patristic_distance_matrix` builds `clades = {clade.name: clade for clade in tree.get_terminals()}` (line 2366) then does `clades[labels[i]]` (line 2371) with no membership check. IQ-TREE's well-documented default behavior removes duplicate/identical sequences from the tree search (only kept with `-keep-ident`, which is not passed in `run_iqtree`'s subprocess args at lines 2353-2354), so a species with any duplicate CDS across S/M/L can produce a treefile missing a label from `labels`, raising an uncaught KeyError. `run_phylogenetics_stage` (def at 2555) calls `_analyze_species` in a plain loop at line 2595-2596 with no try/except, and `run_pipeline`'s call at line 3294 (`phylo_rows = run_phylogenetics_stage(...)`) is likewise unwrapped, and there is no try/except anywhere in `run_pipeline` or `main` (confirmed by reading lines 3368-3381), so the KeyError propagates and aborts the whole run before the 'Writing outputs' block at line 3301, which writes ortho_accession_table and the other core tables.

Same structural gap as [0], described more broadly: lines 2504-2551 (Phylo.read, tree_divergence_for_species, the dendropy RF block at 2512-2525, and the per-member classify_reassortment_call/bootstrap_support_for_pair loop at 2527-2551) all sit after the try/except that ends at line 2503, so any exception there (e.g. bootstrap_support_for_pair's `next(tree.find_clades(name=label_a))` at line 2417 raising StopIteration, or a dendropy TaxonNamespace/encode_bipartitions failure at lines 2512-2519) is uncaught. run_phylogenetics_stage's per-species loop (2593-2596) and its call site in run_pipeline (line 3294) have no surrounding try/except, and main()/run_pipeline have none either (verified lines 3368-3381 and the run_pipeline body around 3290-3309), so the crash happens before 'Writing outputs' (line 3301) and no parquet tables at all are written for that invocation, contradicting the stated per-unit isolation invariant.

In _analyze_species (all_hanta.py ~2496-2503), only run_mafft/run_iqtree are wrapped: `try: run_mafft(...); treefile = run_iqtree(...) except Exception as exc: ... return [_phylo_row(...,'failed',...) for c in members]`. Immediately after that except block, unwrapped code follows: `trees[segment] = Phylo.read(str(treefile), 'newick')` (line 2504), the dendropy TaxonNamespace/Tree.get()/encode_bipartitions()/treecompare.symmetric_difference() block (lines 2512-2525), and classify_reassortment_call -> bootstrap_support_for_pair's `next(tree.find_clades(name=label_a))` (line 2417, which raises StopIteration if no match) -- none of these are inside a try/except. run_phylogenetics_stage calls `_analyze_species(...)` in a plain for-loop with no try/except (`rows.extend(_analyze_species(species, members, ...))`, lines 2593-2596). In run_pipeline, the phylogenetics block (`if args.phylogenetics: ... phylo_rows = run_phylogenetics_stage(...); safe_write_parquet(...)`) runs with no enclosing try/except and is placed before `logging.info("Writing outputs")` and all subsequent safe_write_parquet calls for ortho_accession_table, ortho_species_table, etc. main() also has no try/except around run_pipeline. So any exception raised in the unwrapped post-tree-build code for any one species propagates uncaught all the way out of main(), crashing the process before any output table is written -- exactly as described.

In run_phylogenetics_stage, rows for species that fall below --phylo-min-taxa are built with: `_phylo_row(c, c.isolate.species_name, 0, "species_below_min_taxa", "") for c in candidates if c.isolate.isolate_key not in grouped_keys` (all_hanta.py:2588) -- the third positional arg to _phylo_row (n_taxa_in_tree, mapped to the output column `n_taxa_in_species_tree` at line 2448) is a hardcoded literal 0 regardless of how many candidates that species actually had. group_candidates_by_species (lines 2281-2302) does compute len(members) per species and even logs it via species_drop_reasons (e.g. 'only {len(members)} candidate(s), need {min_taxa}' at line 2299), but that count is never threaded back to the per-isolate row -- only the formatted log string is returned in the Counter, not a species->count mapping usable by _phylo_row. So every isolate belonging to an under-threshold species gets n_taxa_in_species_tree=0 in ortho_reassortment_table.parquet, whether the species actually had 0, 1, or phylo_min_taxa-1 candidates, exactly as the finding describes.

The specific StopIteration mechanism is unreachable given the code path that must execute first. `tree_divergence_for_species` (line 2376) loops `for segment, tree in trees.items(): dist = _patristic_distance_matrix(tree, labels)` (line 2388) over ALL segments including M, using the exact same `labels` list and the exact same `trees["M"]` object that is later passed to `classify_reassortment_call(row, trees["M"], ...)` at line 2530. Inside `_patristic_distance_matrix`, `clades = {clade.name: clade for clade in tree.get_terminals()}` followed by `clades[labels[i]]` / `clades[labels[j]]` dict lookups (lines 2366-2371) already require every label in `labels` to exist as a terminal-clade name in that same M tree object -- if any label were missing, this would raise KeyError here, unguarded, before `classify_reassortment_call` is ever reached (execution wouldn't even get to line 2530). Since execution does reach `classify_reassortment_call` (i.e. `tree_divergence_for_species` returned successfully), every label in `labels` -- including `row["label"]` and `row["tree_m_nearest"] = labels[m_nn]` (line 2401), both drawn from the same `labels` list -- is already proven present as a terminal in `trees["M"]`. `find_clades(name=X)` traverses all clades (terminal and internal) and will therefore always find at least the terminal already confirmed by `get_terminals()`, so `next(...)` in `bootstrap_support_for_pair` (line 2417-2418) cannot raise StopIteration on this call path. The premised trigger (a tip-name variant or off-by-one causing the label to not match) is factually excluded by the prior, unguarded, equivalent lookup over the identical tree object and label set earlier in the same function call chain.
